Correlations between traits in each population

Source: vignettes/articles/correlations-between-traits.Rmd
correlations-between-traits.Rmd

中文版

Two-trait models give the genetic correlation (rg) and the phenotypic correlation (rp) between two traits measured on the same animals. With several populations, they are estimated for every pair of traits in every population.

Data and trait pairs 

library(asreml)
library(mintyr)
library(mintyrasr)

pairs <- c2p_nest(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), by = "test_herd", out_type = "df")
pairs                                    # pairs ("adg-bf", ...) | test_herd | data (value1, value2)

In pairs = "adg-bf", value1 is adg and value2 is bf. param keeps the names h2_value1 / h2_value2; the accuracy, pred and gebv tables use the trait names.

Fit every pair in every population 

res <- asr_gblup(pairs, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, inbreeding = inbreeding,
                 test_rg = TRUE, test_rp = TRUE, path = "correlations_by_herd.xlsx")
res$param[, .(pairs, test_herd, rg, rg_se, rg_p, rp, rp_se, cov_p,
              h2_value1, h2_value2, status)]
column meaning
rg, rg_se genetic correlation Cov_a / sqrt(Va1 Va2)
rp, rp_se phenotypic correlation: all covariances / sqrt(Vp1 Vp2)
rg_p LRT of rg = 0: us(trait) against idh(trait) for the genetic term, boundary = FALSE
cov_p LRT of all covariances = 0 (test_rp = TRUE): are the traits correlated at all
h2_value1, h2_value2 heritabilities of the two traits from the two-trait model

The model is cbind(value1, value2) ~ trait + trait:hhys, us(trait):vm(id, ginv), units:us(trait). The residual covariance needs animals with records of both traits; it is part of rp.

All populations together 

pairs_all <- c2p_nest(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), out_type = "df")
res_all <- asr_gblup(pairs_all, ginv = ginv, fixed = ~ hhys, inbreeding = inbreeding)

A correlation matrix per population

Genetic correlations above the diagonal, phenotypic below:

library(data.table)
p <- copy(res$param)[, c("t1", "t2") := tstrsplit(pairs, "-", fixed = TRUE)]
cor_matrix <- function(herd) {
  x <- p[test_herd == herd]
  tr <- unique(c(x$t1, x$t2))
  m <- diag(1, length(tr)); dimnames(m) <- list(tr, tr)
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(x))) {
    i <- match(x$t1[k], tr); j <- match(x$t2[k], tr)
    m[min(i, j), max(i, j)] <- x$rg[k]        # upper: rg
    m[max(i, j), min(i, j)] <- x$rp[k]        # lower: rp
  }
  round(m, 2)
}
cor_matrix("nls")

When a model does not converge

  • rg close to +-1 or traits with few joint records: try genetic_cov = "corgh" (the correlation is a parameter of its own and its SE comes directly).
  • More iterations: max_update (default 2) continues with update().
  • Fits that still do not converge are skipped and listed in res$log (nonconv = "keep" to use them anyway).
  • An LRT with df = 0 (a parameter restrained or at a bound) gives rg_p = NA with an entry in the log, not a misleading p = 0.

Cross-validation of the two-trait models

The same pairs with cross-validation are the mt_sp (per population) and mt_mp (populations together) scenarios of cv_scenarios():

sc  <- cv_scenarios(pheno, cols = c("adg", "bf", "fcr"), id = "id", group = "test_herd",
                    v = 5, repeats = 5, seed = 2026, scenarios = c("mt_sp", "mt_mp"),
                    out_type = "df")
res <- asr_scenarios(sc, ginv, scenarios = c("mt_sp", "mt_mp"), fixed = ~ hhys)
